title: IFN-γ, IL-12, and Mendelian susceptibility
dek: The IL-12 / IFN-γ / STAT1 axis is the Mendelian proof that human TB control is a Th1 cytokine problem. IGRAs are a laboratory echo of the same axis.
story: Macrophages infected with Mtb make IL-12 (and IL-23). Lymphocytes — especially CD4 T cells and NK cells — answer with IFN-γ. IFN-γ through IFNGR1/2 and STAT1 activates macrophage killing programmes (reactive nitrogen/oxygen, autophagy, antigen presentation). TNF, from macrophages and T cells, maintains granuloma structure.

Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (MSMD) is the human knockout series: IFNGR1, IFNGR2, IL12B, IL12RB1, STAT1, NEMO, and others. Children with these lesions get BCG-osis and NTM, and they teach that the axis is not optional. They are rare; HIV is the common acquired phenocopy.

IGRAs measure IFN-γ (or IFN-γ-secreting cells) after ESAT-6/CFP-10 stimulation. They are an assay of the axis, not a burden assay. Anergy from HIV, steroids, or anti-IFN biologics produces false negatives; that is immunology, not a lab error by default.
deepTitle: What a TB lab should not over-call
deep: Anti-IFN-γ autoantibodies in adults (especially some East- and Southeast-Asian cohorts) produce an acquired MSMD phenocopy with NTM and sometimes TB. Worth knowing when an adult presents like a pediatric cytokine defect.
JAK-STAT inhibitors and anti-IFN biologics are iatrogenic holes in the same axis. Screen and consider TPT the way you already do for anti-TNF.
Host GWAS hits (e.g. HLA, WASF3, ASIPs in some studies) are population priors, not individual DST.
Do not order an IGRA to diagnose meningitis or to follow treatment response. The axis does not report CFU.

visual.caption: IL-12 from infected macrophages licenses IFN-γ from lymphocytes; IFN-γ and TNF return to the macrophage/granuloma. MSMD and HIV break this loop at different joints.

example.title: IGRA-negative miliary TB in advanced HIV
example.setup: CD4 18, miliary pattern, Xpert Ultra trace on sputum, IGRA negative. Colleague calls the IGRA “reassuring against TB.”

steps.title: The axis is broken
steps.body: No CD4 help, exhausted IFN-γ. IGRA can be negative with high burden.

steps.title: Disease tests are NAAT/culture/LAM
steps.body: Ultra trace here is a disease clue, not cancelled by IGRA.

steps.title: Do not delay
steps.body: Treat disease algorithms. IGRA is the wrong tool.

example.takeaway: IFN-γ assays need an IFN-γ axis.

check.prompt: MSMD lesions (IFNGR1, IL12RB1, STAT1, …) teach that:
choices: The IL-12/IFN-γ axis is required for mycobacterial control in humans
BCG is safe in complete IFNGR deficiency
check.answer: The IL-12/IFN-γ axis is required for mycobacterial control in humans
check.why: Human knockouts are the proof, not a mouse-only story.

check.prompt: QFT reports IFN-γ IU/mL in antigen minus nil tubes. A patient on high-dose steroids has nil 0.02, mitogen 0.3 (low), TB antigen 0.15. The correct first read is:
choices: Indeterminate / invalid because the positive-control (mitogen) axis failed — do not call negative
check.answer: Indeterminate / invalid because the positive-control (mitogen) axis failed — do not call negative
check.why: Mitogen failure means you did not demonstrate an intact IFN-γ machinery.

check.prompt: On the cytokine map, what sits between IFN-γ and the infected macrophage?
check.why: Receptor and transcription factor of the IFN-γ response.
